introduction: Registering a property in Tamil Nadu is now a highly digitized process through the STAR 3.0 system on the TNREGINET portal. While the application and payment are online, a physical visit to the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) is typically required for biometric verification, though new "Anywhere Registration" rules are rolling out in late 2026 for specific cases.
quickFacts:
Important to Know (2026 Updates)
  • Total Cost: 11% of the property's market value (or guideline value, whichever is higher):
    • Stamp Duty: 7%
    • Registration Fee: 4%
    • Concession: Women buyers get a 1% reduction on the Registration Fee (paying 3%) for properties valued up to ₹10 Lakhs.
  • Time Taken: Registered documents are typically returned on the same day or within 3 days.
  • Key Portal: TNREGINET
  • New Rule: From August 17, 2026, a new "Anywhere Registration" system will allow builders/promoters to register first-sale properties completely online without visiting the SRO. For most resales (buying from an individual), a physical visit is still standard.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Property Registration

Requirement: You must have the original copies of these documents during your Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) visit.
Core Deeds & Titles
  • Sale Deed: Legal draft prepared by a document writer or advocate on stamp paper (physical or e-stamp).
  • Parent Documents: Original sale deeds of the previous owners to trace ownership history.
  • Encumbrance Certificate (EC): Proof that the property has no legal dues or mortgages.
Revenue & Tax Records
  • Patta / Chitta / Adangal: Revenue records proving land ownership and classification.
  • Building Plan Approval: Needed if registering a constructed house/apartment.
  • Property Tax Receipts: Latest payment receipts.
  • Patta Transfer Application: Often submitted along with the registration (or integrated).
Personal Identification & Photos
  • ID Proofs: Aadhaar Card and PAN Card for both Buyer and Seller (PAN is mandatory for transactions > ₹10 Lakhs).
  • Passport Size Photos: Recent photographs of both buyer and seller.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Registration & Fee Payment

Mandatory Step: All registrations must be initiated online. You cannot walk into an office with paper forms anymore.
Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Register on TNREGINET: Go to tnreginet.gov.in. Click "Registration" -> "User Registration" to create an account.
  2. Calculate & Pay Fees: Use the portal's "Guideline Value" search to check your property's official value. The system will calculate the Stamp Duty (7%) and Registration Fee (4%). Pay these charges online via the portal (Netbanking/UPI) or generate a challan to pay at a bank.
  3. Draft & Upload: Click "Create Document" to draft your Sale Deed online or have a document writer do it. Upload scanned PDF copies of all required documents (ID, Parent Deed, Patta, etc.).
  4. Book Appointment: Once the Sub-Registrar approves the draft (usually within 24 hours), you will get an option to select a time slot. Book a "Token" for your visit to the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO).
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Physical SRO Visit (Document Execution)

Note: "Offline Application" now refers to the physical execution step. You cannot apply manually from scratch.
On the Appointment Day:
  1. Arrive on Time: Reach the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) 15 minutes before your token time.
  2. Submission: Hand over the printed receipt of your online payment and the original documents to the officer.
  3. Biometrics & Photography:
    • Couples/Parties: Both Buyer and Seller must be present to give thumb impressions and have photos taken via the webcam.
    • Witnesses: Two witnesses must also be present with their ID proofs to sign and provide thumb impressions.
  4. Verification: The Registrar will verify the details and sign the deed.
  5. Collect Receipt: You will receive a receipt number to track your document.
afterApplying:
After Registration — Post-Submission Details

Collect Document & Digital Copy

The registered Sale Deed is scanned and uploaded to the portal. You can typically collect the original physical copy on the same day or within 3 days from the SRO. You can also log in to TNREGINET and download a digitally signed certified copy of your deed.

Patta Transfer
  • For many transactions, the Patta transfer is now automatically triggered. You will receive an SMS or can track it online.
  • If not automatic, apply for a name transfer at the local Taluk office or via the e-Sevai center using your new Sale Deed.
